title: Ossie field-level saiku.roles is bypassed by naming the physical column; GraphQL and semantic export return the unfiltered model

criteria.given: a caller whose roles deny (or do not allow) an Ossie field names the field's physical column in rows, in a filters entry with or without dataset, or in sorts
criteria.then: the translator (OssieRoleContext.assertShelfVisible, called before SQL emission) resolves every row, filter and sort identifier against the caller's role-filtered model and refuses the request (SaikuAccessDeniedException for a denied known field, SaikuValidationException for a name that is no visible field/metric of the model) — an unresolvable identifier never falls through to a raw quoted column

criteria.given: an identifier that is not a field or metric of the model is submitted by any caller
criteria.then: it is rejected as a typed 400 (SaikuValidationException) on /api/query/execute, /preview-sql and the /execute-async path, not a 500 and not a raw SQL column emission

criteria.given: a caller whose roles hide fields/metrics reads GraphQL ossieModel, GET /ai/ossie/export/{connection}/{tool} or /ai/ossie/ontology/{connection}/{model}
criteria.then: the response is built from OssieRoleContext.filterHidden (the caller's role-filtered view) and the GraphQL fetcher applies the schema-metadata AI policy guard, same as REST GET /ai/ossie/schema

unit tests cover OssieRoleContext identifier resolution (unknown/denied for rows, unqualified filters, sorts by field and by metric, values) and one end-to-end test through a real OSSIE datasource proves the physical-column bypass is closed on the execute path
